title: One Geometry, Different Outcomes: Readout-Dependent Effects of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.36101v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Contrastive vision-language models learn shared embedding spaces by aligning matched image-text pairs, yet their representations remain separated by a modality gap. Prior work reports divergent effects of modifying this gap: reducing it can improve zero-shot classification and cross-modal alignment, whereas removing gap-related structure can degrade image-text retrieval. In this paper, we provide a unified geometric explanation for these task-dependent effects. Across CLIP and SigLIP encoders, we find that a single dominant direction captures 94.4-99.9% of the squared norm of the image-text mean separation, revealing that the mean-separation component is approximately rank-one. A decomposition of the similarity score then identifies three task-specific roles. translated_title: 一种几何，不同结果：视觉-语言模型中模态鸿沟的读出依赖效应
translated_abstract: 对比视觉-语言模型通过对齐匹配的图像-文本对来学习共享嵌入空间，但其表示仍被模态鸿沟分隔开。先前的研究报告了对这一鸿沟进行修改时产生的分歧效果：减小该鸿沟可以提升零样本分类和跨模态对齐性能，而移除与鸿沟相关的结构则可能损害图像-文本检索效果。在本文中，我们为这些任务依赖的效应提供了统一的几何解释。在CLIP和SigLIP编码器上，我们发现单一主导方向即可捕获图像-文本均值分离平方范数的94.4-99.9%，这表明均值分离分量近似为秩一结构。随后对相似度分数进行分解，识别出三种任务特定的角色。在零样本分类中，查询侧固定的鸿沟偏移减除恰好等价于一个加性类别偏置。在标准跨模态检索中，投影去除鸿沟方向……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文发现视觉-语言模型中模态鸿沟的均值分离分量在几何上近似为秩一结构，并通过对相似度分数的分解解释了为何修改该鸿沟会在零样本分类与跨模态检索等不同任务中产生截然相反的效果，提供了统一的几何解释。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that the modality gap in vision-language models is approximately rank-one geometrically, and by decomposing the similarity score, provides a unified geometric explanation for why modifying the gap produces divergent effects across tasks such as zero-shot classification and cross-modal retrieval.
